variables.reason: The ledger definition for Ra is “the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations” which matches the canonical quantity ‘arithmetic mean roughness’ (entry_id pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness). That record’s definition explicitly states Ra is a dimensional roughness-height statistic with si_unit m and si_dimension L, so every known coordinate of the candidate vector (length = 1, all other base exponents = 0) is supported. The cited record applies to the original problem because it defines the same statistical measure of surface height used as an input for sand-grain roughness parameterization and uses the same symbol Ra; it therefore justifies treating Ra as a length quantity.

The ledger defines kt as ‘the peak-to-valley height’ which corresponds to the canonical ‘mean peak-to-valley roughness height’ (entry_id pq_peak_to_valley_height). That record describes a vertical height difference between peaks and valleys and assigns si_unit m and si_dimension L. Because the original problem’s kt is an amplitude (height) measure of the surface, the cited record directly establishes that kt carries units of length; the candidate vector (L = 1, others = 0) is therefore correct.

k_rms is described in the ledger as ‘the root-mean-square height of the surface roughness’, matching the canonical ‘root-mean-square roughness height’ (entry_id pq_rms_roughness_height). That entry defines k_rms as the RMS fluctuation of surface height about its mean, with si_unit m and si_dimension L. Because the original variable is exactly that RMS height statistic used in roughness parameterization, the candidate vector (length = 1, others = 0) is fully supported.

The ledger defines Sk as ‘the third central moment of roughness height fluctuations divided by the cube of their root-mean-square height’, i.e. the standardized third moment (skewness). The canonical record pq_height_skewness describes Sk as a dimensionless standardized moment with si_unit 1 and si_dimension 1 (no base exponents). This matches the original problem’s role of Sk as a shape factor of the height distribution, so the candidate vector (all base exponents = 0) is justified.

Ku is given as the kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations in the ledger; the canonical record pq_height_kurtosis defines this as the fourth standardized moment, explicitly dimensionless with si_unit 1. Because the original Ku is a statistical shape parameter (kurtosis) of the height distribution used in the parameterization, the candidate vector (all zeros) is supported by the cited record.

ES is defined in the ledger as ‘the effective streamwise slope of the roughness’—the mean absolute gradient of surface height in a horizontal direction. The canonical entry pq_effective_surface_slope states that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and is therefore dimensionless (si_unit 1). Because the original variable ES is explicitly a slope (gradient) of height used in flow roughness characterization, the candidate vector (all zeros) is consistent with that physical meaning.

Po is listed as ‘surface porosity’ in the ledger and the canonical record pq_porosity defines porosity as a fraction (void fraction) with si_unit 1 and dimensionless. The entry explicitly states it is a fraction of area/volume and the dataset note to confirm exact geometric definition does not change its dimensionless character. Thus the candidate vector (all base exponents = 0) is supported for Po.

candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The problem states to derive the dimensionless relationship governing the normalized equivalent sand-grain roughness ks/Ra using the given input parameters. ks/Ra is dimensionless because it is a ratio of two lengths (ks and Ra). The input parameters include length scales (Ra, kt, k_rms), dimensionless shape factors (Sk, Ku), a slope (ES), and porosity (Po), which is also dimensionless. Therefore, the output ks/Ra is dimensionless.

Because the original problem’s kt is an amplitude (height) measure of the surface, the cited record directly establishes that kt carries units of length; the candidate vector (L = 1, others = 0) is therefore correct.

k_rms is described in the ledger as ‘the root-mean-square height of the surface roughness’, matching the canonical ‘root-mean-square roughness height’ (entry_id pq_rms_roughness_height). Because the original variable is exactly that RMS height statistic used in roughness parameterization, the candidate vector (length = 1, others = 0) is fully supported.

The ledger defines Sk as ‘the third central moment of roughness height fluctuations divided by the cube of their root-mean-square height’, i.e. the standardized third moment (skewness). This matches the original problem’s role of Sk as a shape factor of the height distribution, so the candidate vector (all base exponents = 0) is justified.

Ku is given as the kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations in the ledger; the canonical record pq_height_kurtosis defines this as the fourth standardized moment, explicitly dimensionless with si_unit 1. Because the original Ku is a statistical shape parameter (kurtosis) of the height distribution used in the parameterization, the candidate vector (all zeros) is supported by the cited record.

ES is defined in the ledger as ‘the effective streamwise slope of the roughness’—the mean absolute gradient of surface height in a horizontal direction. The canonical entry pq_effective_surface_slope states that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and is therefore dimensionless (si_unit 1). Because the original variable ES is explicitly a slope (gradient) of height used in flow roughness characterization, the candidate vector (all zeros) is consistent with that physical meaning.

Po is listed as ‘surface porosity’ in the ledger and the canonical record pq_porosity defines porosity as a fraction (void fraction) with si_unit 1 and dimensionless. The entry explicitly states it is a fraction of area/volume and the dataset note to confirm exact geometric definition does not change its dimensionless character. Problem:
Perform dimensional analysis for sand-grain roughness parameterization to derive the dimensionless relationship governing the normalized equivalent sand-grain roughness (denoted as ks/Ra).
This analysis uses ONLY the following 7 physical quantities as input parameters:
the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations, Ra;
the peak-to-valley height, kt;
the root-mean-square height, k_rms;
the third central moment of roughness height fluctuations divided by the cube of their root-mean-square height, Sk;
the kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations, Ku;
the effective streamwise slope of the roughness, ES;
the surface porosity, Po.
